source_passages.quotation: **Rule (2.5):** A player rules a clearing with more total **warriors plus buildings** than each other player. Tokens and pawns do not contribute. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules. Eyrie rule a tie for most if they have at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or stop someone else ruling.

answer.ruling: More warriors plus buildings than each opponent rules; tokens/pawns don’t count. Ordinary tie means nobody. Eyrie wins tied-most with at least one piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or prevent rule.

source_passages.quotation: **Move (4.2):** Take any positive number of your warriors/pawns from one clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing. You must rule origin or destination or both. Recheck rule for each move. You may move the same pieces repeatedly, including on multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly treats them as paths. Moving and placing are different procedures. Vagabond has its own movement exceptions below.

answer.ruling: Move positive number from clearing along linking path to adjacent clearing; rule origin or destination or both, rechecking each move. Same pieces can move repeatedly. River is not path unless effect says so.

source_passages.quotation:
**Battle (4.3):** Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. **Battle does not require you to rule the clearing.** Resolve these six steps:

1. **Ambush:** Defender may play one ambush matching clearing (birds are wild). Attacker may foil it with a matching ambush. Defender’s card is discarded; a foiled ambush deals no hits. Otherwise defender immediately deals two hits, then discards ambush. If no attacking warriors or pawns remain, battle ends immediately. Ambush hits are not limited by defending warriors.
2. **Before-roll effects:** Resolve applicable effects; attacker chooses order if both have them.
3. **Roll:** Higher die is attacker’s rolled hits, lower defender’s; equal dice give equal results. Each side’s rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle. Alliance defending reverses the dice; Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors.
4. **After-roll effects:** Resolve effects affecting battle that do not say “before rolling”; attacker chooses order if both have them.
5. **Count hits:** Add extra hits (uncapped by warriors), subtract ignored hits. If defender has no warriors, attacker deals one extra hit for **defenseless**; Vagabond is instead defenseless if it has no undamaged swords.
6. **Deal hits:** Each hit removes one opposing piece. The side taking hits chooses its own removal order, but **all its warriors must be removed before its buildings/tokens**. It also chooses order of effects triggered by its pieces’ removal. Both sides deal their counted hits; losing warriors does not retroactively change the rolled cap. Whoever removes an enemy building/token scores **one VP each**, even while defending and even outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage instead.

answer.ruling: Choose a clearing with your warriors/pawn and enemy defender; ruling not required. Ambush may be foiled by matching attacker ambush (birds wild); unfoiled ambush deals two immediate hits and battle ends if no attacker pawns/warriors remain. Attacker orders same-timing before/after effects. High die attacker, low defender, ties equal; rolled hits capped by own warriors, Alliance defense reverses dice, Vagabond uses undamaged swords. Add extra hits, subtract ignored hits; extra hits uncapped. Defenseless adds hit if defender no warriors, or Vagabond has no undamaged swords. Hit side chooses removals but must remove all warriors before buildings/tokens; it orders removal triggers. Both deal counted hits. Remover of enemy building/token scores 1 VP, even defending/outside battle; Vagabond takes hits as item damage.

source_passages.quotation:
**Craft (4.1):** **Every crafting piece gets its suit from the clearing containing it.** The card’s **bottom-left crafting icons** require pieces of those clearing suits; the card’s own suit does not define the cost. Craft a card from hand when your faction permits.

**Personal duplicate check:** Only an identical persistent effect **in your own play area** prevents you from crafting that effect again. Other players’ copies do not count for this duplicate restriction.

- **Marquise, Eyrie and Alliance cost:** For **each icon**, activate **one workshop, roost or sympathy in a clearing matching that icon’s suit**, respectively. A crafting piece gets its suit from its clearing. Combine eligible pieces as needed, but **each piece may activate only once per turn**.
- **Vagabond cost and reuse:** The pawn **may activate repeatedly in a turn**. For each icon, **pay by exhausting one face-up, undamaged hammer: flip that hammer face down**. The pawn’s **current clearing must match every icon on the card**. Reusing the pawn never waives the hammer payment per icon. One clearing cannot pay mixed fox/rabbit/mouse icons.
- A **three-color question-mark icon** accepts any suit.

- Immediate effect (paper box): resolve, then discard the **crafting card**. An item card requires the corresponding **item token** in the map supply, or it cannot be crafted.

answer.part: Craft cost, piece reuse, supply, duplicate
answer.ruling: Every bottom-left icon costs a matching-suit crafting piece (suit from clearing). Marquise/Eyrie/Alliance use workshop/roost/sympathy per icon, each piece once/turn. Vagabond flips one face-up undamaged hammer per icon; pawn current clearing must match all icons and is reusable; question-mark accepts any suit. Missing item token supply means cannot craft. Only own-play-area identical persistent effect bars a duplicate.

source_passages.quotation: **Dominance (3.3):** In own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate a dominance card from hand into play area; remove score marker and stop scoring VP. Cannot remove/replace activated card. At **start of own Birdsong**, win if ruling **three clearings of matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit**, or for **bird dominance, two diagonally opposite corner clearings**. Meeting condition earlier does not immediately win.

answer.ruling: In own Daylight at 10+ VP activate from hand, remove score marker, stop VP scoring. At start own Birdsong win by ruling three matching mouse/rabbit/fox clearings or two diagonally opposite corners for bird; earlier meeting does not win. Activated card cannot be removed/replaced.

source_passages.quotation: Dominance cards cannot be crafted, but can be spent for suit. Whenever one would enter discard, put it near map available instead. During own Daylight, spend matching card to take available dominance into hand. Available **bird dominance remains bird**, so payment must be bird; a bird hand card can pay for non-bird dominance. Activation and taking are separate, neither requires a faction action allowance.

answer.ruling: A spent dominance card goes near map as available instead of discard. During own Daylight spend matching card to take available card to hand; bird dominance still requires bird. Taking and activating are separate and neither needs faction action allowance.

source_passages.quotation:
**Setup:** Use **Standard Setup**, in this order (Law 5.1):

1. Choose factions; determine starting player and seating randomly. Take faction boards and their listed pieces. Use Fall or Winter. Fall has no special rules; on Winter, the river divides forests just as printed paths do. Rivers are otherwise not paths.
2. Put score markers at 0.
3. With two players, remove all four dominance cards. Shuffle shared deck; each player draws **three cards**.
4. **Ruins and items:** Cover the four R building slots with ruins. The separate map item supply is **2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, 2 coins**. Keep the four R-marked ruin items separate from this supply: only Vagabond faction setup hides one each of its R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword beneath the four ruins, **one item beneath each ruin**. During that Vagabond setup, shuffle the ruin/item stacks and return each to an empty R ruin slot, keeping item identities hidden. Without a Vagabond, ruins contain no items.
7. Set up factions in their letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. Setup order is distinct from turn order.

answer.ruling: Remove four dominance cards for 2 players; shuffle deck and draw three each. Cover four R slots with ruins. Supply 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, 2 coins. If Vagabond, hide one R bag/boot/hammer/sword under each ruin after shuffling stacks hidden; without Vagabond no ruin items. Faction setup order Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond.

source_passages.quotation: **Keep:** Only Marquise may **place** pieces in its clearing; other players may **move** pieces into it. The keep cannot be placed again if removed. **Field Hospitals:** Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the keep clearing instead of supply. This can apply outside battle. Without a keep there is no destination for hospitals.

answer.ruling: Only Marquise may place pieces in Keep clearing; others may move into it. Keep cannot be placed again if removed. When Marquise warriors removed from a clearing, may spend one matching card to place them in Keep instead of supply; applies outside battle. No Keep means no hospital destination.

source_passages.quotation:
**Daylight:** First craft with workshops. Then take **up to three actions**, plus **one per bird card spent outside an action**, in any order and number except Recruit’s limit:

- **Battle:** One battle.
- **March:** Up to two moves; either may use the same or different warriors. Do not interrupt the compound action to spend a bird card or take another action.
- **Recruit:** One warrior at **each recruiter**; only **once per turn**. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters.
- **Overwork:** Spend a card matching a sawmill’s clearing to place one wood there.

answer.ruling: Craft with workshops first, then up to three actions plus one per bird spent outside action. Battle one; March up to two moves without interruption; Recruit one per recruiter once/turn; Overwork matching clearing card places wood at sawmill.

source_passages.quotation: - **Build:** Choose a clearing you rule with open slot and choose building type. Take the leftmost building of that type. Pay cost shown atop its column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or from other ruled clearings linked to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place building; score VP on uncovered space. You cannot build without full wood cost, the building and legal slot.

answer.ruling: Choose ruled clearing with open slot and building type; take leftmost building of type; pay column cost using wood in target or other ruled clearings linked by unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place and score uncovered space VP. Full cost, building and legal slot required.

source_passages.quotation:
**Birdsong, in order:**

1. **Emergency Orders:** If hand empty, draw one.
2. **Add to Decree:** Must add one or two hand cards, **at most one added bird card**. Each goes to any column; columns have no size limit.
3. **A New Roost:** If no roosts on map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors **where all these pieces can be placed**.

answer.ruling: Emergency Orders draw one if hand empty. Add one/two card to Decree, at most one bird, any column. If no roosts, place roost plus three warriors in clearing with fewest warriors where all pieces can be placed.

source_passages.quotation:
**Daylight — resolve the Decree:** Craft using roosts first, then resolve **every Decree card**, column by column **Recruit → Move → Battle → Build**. Within one column choose card order freely. Bird is wild. **If any required action cannot be fully completed, immediately enter Turmoil: you cannot skip the card or continue other columns.** Each card requires:

| Decree column | Match the card’s suit to | Required procedure for one card |
|---|---|---|
| Recruit | Clearing with a roost | Place **one warrior at one chosen roost** there; Charismatic must instead place **two warriors** there |
| Move | Origin clearing | Move **at least one warrior**, obeying ordinary path and rule requirements |
| Battle | Clearing of battle | Initiate a battle there with Eyrie warriors and an enemy |
| Build | Target clearing | Place one roost in a clearing you rule, with an open slot and **no roost already there** |

**Bird Decree cards are wild in every column:** choose any clearing suit, while still meeting that action’s other requirements.

If any required action cannot be completed fully for any reason (including warrior/building supply), immediately enter **Turmoil**; do not skip that card or continue other Decree columns.

answer.ruling: Craft first, then columns Recruit→Move→Battle→Build; any order within column. Recruit card suit at roost clearing, one warrior at one chosen roost (Charismatic two). Move suit at origin, move ≥1 obeying normal. Battle suit battle clearing with Eyrie warriors vs enemy. Build suit target clearing, place roost where Eyrie rules, open slot, no roost. Bird wild. Failure to complete fully causes immediate Turmoil; cannot skip/continue.

source_passages.quotation: **Turmoil, in order:** Lose one VP per bird Decree card **including both Loyal Viziers**; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement. If none face up, flip all leaders face up before choosing. Retuck Viziers in new leader’s columns. End Daylight and proceed to the full normal Evening: **score the roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, then discard to five**. **Turmoil does not remove your map warriors or buildings.**

answer.ruling: Lose VP per bird Decree card including Viziers; discard all Decree except Viziers; flip current leader face down, choose face-up replacement (if none flip all face up); retuck Viziers. End Daylight, then normal Evening score/draw/discard. Map warriors/buildings remain.

source_passages.quotation: **Outrage:** Each time another player **removes sympathy** or **moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing**, that player adds one matching hand card (birds count) to Supporters. Moving a group costs one card per affected move, rather than one per warrior. If no matching cards including birds, show hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. **If Supporters is full, discard the incoming Outrage card; payment or the no-match draw still occurs.** Merely battling there is no trigger unless sympathy is removed; placing warriors there and moving only Vagabond pawn do not trigger it.

answer.ruling: Another player removing sympathy or moving warriors into it triggers one matching hand card per affected move (birds count), not per warrior. No match: reveal hand to Alliance, Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. Full stack discards incoming card but payment/draw happens. Battle alone no trigger absent sympathy removal; placing warriors and only Vagabond pawn movement do not trigger.

source_passages.quotation:
**Birdsong:** Both Revolt and Spread Sympathy take place **during Birdsong**. Complete **all Revolts before starting any Spread Sympathy**; each may be performed any number of times. **For both actions, every supporter spent must match the target clearing; birds are wild.** Once spreading starts, you cannot return to Revolt this Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt:

- **Revolt:** Choose sympathetic clearing without a base, matching a base still on your board. Spend **two matching supporters**. **Remove all enemy pieces there and score one VP per enemy building/token removed**; then place matching base. Place warriors there equal to number of sympathetic clearings matching the base’s printed suit (including revolt clearing), and one warrior in Officers box. Score normal VP for removed enemy buildings/tokens. Enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed.
- **Spread Sympathy:** Choose unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy; if no sympathy anywhere, choose any clearing. Spend matching supporters shown above next sympathy token. **Martial Law:** add one matching supporter if chosen clearing has at least three warriors of **one other player**. Place token and score uncovered space. Only one sympathy per clearing.

answer.ruling: Both in Birdsong, all Revolts before any Spread; repeat either. Matching target supporters, birds wild. Revolt: sympathetic clearing without base matching a base on board; spend 2, remove enemies, score buildings/tokens, place base, matching-suit sympathy-count warriors there plus one officer; Vagabond damages three items. Spread: unsympathetic target adjacent by path or any if no sympathy; pay supporters shown plus Martial Law one if ≥3 warriors of one other player; place token, score uncovered VP; one token/clearing. Cannot return to Revolt after spreading starts.

source_passages.quotation:
**Losing a base:** Discard all supporters matching its clearing **including birds**, remove half officers **rounded up**. If no bases remain, discard excess supporters down to five. Do this whenever a base is removed.

- **Train during Daylight:** Spend a **hand card** matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers box. Supporters cannot pay Train. Each officer allows one Evening military operation; taking operations does not consume officers.

Organize spends no supporters and has no sympathy-adjacency requirement or Martial Law cost; it still needs legal token placement.

answer.ruling: Train in Daylight: matching hand card at base clearing puts one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay. Organize removes Alliance warrior from unsympathetic clearing, places sympathy, scores uncovered VP; no supporters, adjacency or Martial Law, but legal placement. Base loss discards matching supporters incl birds, half officers rounded up; if no bases, supporters down to five.

source_passages.quotation:
1. **Refresh:** First count tea **already face up on Refresh track**; flip two exhausted items face up per counted tea, then three more exhausted items. Tea refreshed during this step gives no extra refresh this step. Refreshing changes face, not damaged status.
2. **Slip (optional):** Move to an adjacent clearing or forest, exhausting **no boots**, even into hostile warriors. Ignore all effects preventing movement **out of** a clearing.

- **Move:** Exhaust one boot, plus **one extra boot** if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction (also for forced moves). Ignore rule. **Cannot enter a forest with this action; from a forest you may move only to an adjacent clearing.** Slip has the special free-boot exception.

1. If in forest, **Rest**: return all damaged items to Satchel and flip them face up; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if able. This does not refresh undamaged exhausted items.
2. **Always draw**, even after forest Rest: one card plus one per face-up coins on track.

answer.ruling: Refresh counts face-up tea on Refresh track first: 2 items refreshed each, then 3; newly refreshed tea no extra. Optional Slip moves adjacent clearing/forest without boots, even hostile; ignores effects preventing movement out. Normal Move costs one boot plus one for any hostile-faction warriors at destination; ignores rule, cannot enter forest, forest can only move to adjacent clearing. Forest Rest returns damaged items face-up, moves ready tracks if possible; no undamaged exhausted refresh. Always draw one + face-up coins even after rest.

source_passages.quotation:
- **Explore:** Exhaust torch in ruin’s clearing. Take one hidden item face up into Satchel or track; score one VP if an item taken. Remove ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the building slot.
- **Quest (matching clearing only):** Choose a face-up quest matching clearing; exhaust its **two listed items**, put quest in play area completed. Choose either VP equal to matching completed quests **including this one**, or draw two cards. Draw replacement quest into public display. No cards are spent to pay a quest.
- **Repair:** Exhaust hammer; move one damaged item to Satchel **keeping current face**. Ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space.

answer.ruling: Explore exhaust torch at ruin; take one hidden item face-up, score 1 VP if taken, remove ruin when last item taken and free slot. Quest matching clearing: exhaust listed two items, complete it; either score count of matching completed quests including it or draw two cards; replace quest. Repair exhaust hammer, move one damaged item to Satchel without changing face; ready tea/coins/bags to track if room.

source_passages.quotation:
- **Strike:** Exhaust crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in clearing. Only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another of its faction pieces instead. Check hostility. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
- **Hostile:** Removing **one** warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately moves marker to Hostile (except allied battle-loss rule above). **Infamy:** During battle on your own turn, score **one extra VP per hostile piece removed**, except warrior that first made faction Hostile. **Each hostile building/token removed in battle on your turn normally scores two VP: one removal VP plus one Infamy. A hostile warrior scores one Infamy, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status.** Infamy depends on whose turn it is, rather than which side attacks: no Infamy on another player’s turn, and none from Strike.
- Aid cannot move marker out of Hostile; it can still obtain a crafted item.

answer.ruling: Removing one non-Hostile warrior makes faction Hostile, except allied-loss rule. On own-turn battle score 1 Infamy per Hostile piece removed except triggering warrior; hostile building/token yields 1 ordinary + 1 Infamy; no Infamy other turn or Strike. Aid cannot reset Hostile. Strike exhaust crossbow, remove warrior, and only if faction has no warriors there may remove another piece; no Infamy.

source_passages.quotation: **Vagabond coalition (9.2.8):** Cannot activate normal dominance win. With **four or more players**, during own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate dominance to coalition with another player **not already in coalition**, whose VP is lowest among players other than you (choose among ties). Put your score marker on partner’s faction board and stop scoring. If partner wins, you also win, including if partner wins through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.

answer.ruling: At 4+ players, own Daylight with 10+ VP, choose player not already in coalition with lowest VP among others (tie choose); coalition, put score marker on partner board and stop scoring. Win if partner wins incl dominance. Hostile partner becomes Indifferent.

source_passages.quotation: - **Precedence:** Card overrides Law; Law overrides Learning to Play. Follow general and faction rules together when possible; if incompatible, faction rule wins. **Cannot is absolute** unless explicitly overridden. (1.1.)

answer.ruling: Card > Law > Learning to Play. Apply general and faction rules together; faction wins conflict. Cannot absolute unless explicit override.

source_passages.quotation: An action, ability or persistent effect cannot be interrupted unless an effect explicitly permits it; a Marquise March’s two moves are one compound action. If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order.

answer.ruling: Unclear simultaneous effects decided by turn player; same-timing battle effects ordered by attacker. Marquise March’s two moves are compound action; cannot interrupt to spend bird or take another action.

source_passages.quotation: Take turns clockwise: **Birdsong → Daylight → Evening**. “At start” effects precede all other phase effects; “at end” effects follow everything else in that phase, before next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions.

answer.ruling: At-start effects precede phase effects; at-end effects follow phase effects before next phase. After last step begins, no other actions except expressly end-of-Evening/turn actions.

source_passages.quotation: Hand size is public, contents private: reveal/show only if explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched/inspected; deck cannot. Agreements are non-binding; cards may be transferred only as instructed; actions require no consent. (1.2–3.)

answer.ruling: Hand size public, contents private; reveal only if told. Face-up piles inspectable; deck not. Deals non-binding, transfer cards only as instructed, actions require no consent.

source_passages.quotation: - **Cards:** Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, even for multiple same-suit payments. **If prompted to give or discard cards of a non-bird suit, you must treat your birds as that suit**; the instruction determines how many cards to give or discard. **Only a bird card can pay an explicit bird-card requirement; fox, rabbit and mouse cards cannot pay it.** Draw from shared deck top; when deck empties, immediately shuffle discard into new deck. (2.1.)

answer.ruling: When deck empties, immediately shuffle discard into new deck. Birds substitute for any non-bird, including multiple same-suit; when told to give/discard non-bird suit must treat birds as suit. Explicit bird requirement only paid with bird.

source_passages.quotation: Pieces are finite: no proxies. When an instruction cannot place/take/remove all prompted pieces, **you must do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer**; this never waives costs or prerequisites, nor the Eyrie’s obligation to complete Decree actions.

answer.ruling: Finite pieces, no proxies. If cannot do all prompted, do maximum possible; cannot choose fewer. This does not waive costs/prerequisites or Eyrie full Decree obligations.

source_passages.quotation:
- **Place/remove/replace:** Place normally from supply/leftmost track; remove normally to supply/rightmost **empty** track space, items permanently.
For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects.

answer.ruling: Place from supply/leftmost track; removals to supply/rightmost empty track; items permanently removed. For simultaneous removal, remove all before removal-trigger effects.

source_passages.quotation: - **Force:** Resolve forced actions as if affected player chose them, retaining their abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its battle decisions. (1.5.5.)

answer.ruling: Forced action resolves as if affected player chose, retaining their abilities/restrictions; forced player decides their own battle.

source_passages.quotation: - **Place/remove/replace:** Replace requires both removal and placement possible; the keep’s placement ban cannot be bypassed by replacing an enemy piece. Swap ignores move/place restrictions. (G.5, G.20, G.23–24, G.31, G.33.)

answer.ruling: Replace needs removal and placement possible; Keep placement ban cannot be bypassed by replacing. Swap ignores move/place restrictions.

source_passages.quotation: **30 VP:** First to 30 wins immediately, on any player’s turn. If multiple reach 30 simultaneously, tied player closest clockwise to current player wins, including current player.

answer.ruling: If multiple reach 30 simultaneously, tied player closest clockwise to current player wins, including current player.

source_passages.quotation: Fall has no special rules; on Winter, the river divides forests just as printed paths do. Rivers are otherwise not paths. **Forest adjacency for Slip:** a forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path, and to forests separated by just one printed path. Winter’s river also divides forests.

answer.ruling: Slip forest adjacent to clearings touching without crossing printed path, and forests separated by one printed path; Winter river divides forests too. Fall has no special rules.

source_passages.quotation: **Marquise setup (6.3):** Supply 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put keep in any corner (starting clearing). Put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop and recruiter among the keep clearing and adjacent clearings, in any combination respecting slots. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks from right to left, leaving leftmost space empty.

answer.ruling: Supply 25 warriors/8 wood; Keep any corner; one warrior each clearing except diagonally opposite. One each sawmill/workshop/recruiter among Keep and adjacent clearings respecting slots. Remaining five each type track right-to-left, leftmost empty.

source_passages.quotation: **Eyrie setup (7.3):** Supply 20 warriors. Put one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player’s starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader; keep others face up nearby. Tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into the columns listed on that leader. Fill roost track with the other six roosts from right to left.

answer.ruling: Supply 20. Roost+6 warriors in eligible corner not other start, diagonally opposite if possible. Choose leader; others face-up nearby. Tuck two bird Viziers into leader columns. Other six roosts on track right-to-left.

source_passages.quotation: **Alliance setup (8.3):** Supply 10 warriors. Put the three bases in their matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track. Draw **three additional cards** face down into Supporters; these are separate from your three-card hand. Start with no map pieces or officers.

answer.ruling: Supply 10 warriors; three bases matching board spaces, ten sympathy on track; draw three extra face-down Supporters in addition to hand; no map pieces/officers.

source_passages.quotation: **Vagabond setup (9.3):** Choose Thief, Tinker or Ranger; place pawn in any forest. Shuffle quests and display three face up. Take S-marked starting items listed on character: tea, coins and bags go face up on matching tracks, other items face up in Satchel; return unused S items to box. Place each other faction’s relationship marker at Indifferent.

answer.ruling: Pick character; pawn any forest; shuffle/display 3 quests. Take character S starting items: tea/coins/bags to matching tracks face-up, others Satchel face-up; return unused S items. Other factions Indifferent.

source_passages.quotation: **Recommended faction mix (5.2):** Reach should total at least 17 for two players, 18 for three, 21 for four. Base reach: Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, Alliance 3. The Law allows adventurous groups to use any mix totaling at least 17.

answer.ruling: Minimum guidance: 17 for 2, 18 for 3, 21 for 4. Values: Marquise10, Eyrie7, Vagabond5, Alliance3. Law permits any mix totaling at least17.

source_passages.quotation:
**Wood production:** Birdsong places one wood per sawmill in its clearing. During Daylight, each Overwork action spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there. Both methods draw from the same finite supply of eight wood tokens.

**Evening:** Draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus; discard hand down to five.

answer.ruling: Birdsong one wood per sawmill, finite total eight shared with Overwork. Overwork spends matching card to place one wood at sawmill. Evening draw one plus uncovered bonuses, discard to five.

source_passages.quotation: - **Recruit:** One warrior at **each recruiter**; only **once per turn**. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters.

answer.ruling: Once per turn, one warrior at each recruiter. If insufficient supply, place maximum and choose among eligible recruiters.

source_passages.quotation: **Disdain for Trade:** Crafted items score only **one VP instead of printed VP** (other extra crafting-point effects still apply). Builder ignores Disdain.

answer.ruling: Eyrie craft item scores 1 instead printed, but extra crafting-point effects apply. Builder ignores Disdain.

source_passages.quotation:
| Leader | Vizier columns | Ability |
|---|---|---|
| Builder | Recruit, Move | Ignore Disdain for Trade |
| Charismatic | Recruit, Battle | Each Recruit must place two warriors instead of one |
| Commander | Move, Battle | One extra hit as attacker |
| Despot | Move, Build | When removing at least one enemy building/token in battle, score one extra VP in addition to normal removal points |

answer.ruling: Builder Recruit/Move, ignore Disdain. Charismatic Recruit/Battle, two warriors per Recruit. Commander Move/Battle, extra attacker hit. Despot Move/Build, extra VP if battle removes ≥1 enemy building/token.

source_passages.quotation:
| Recruit | Clearing with a roost | Place **one warrior at one chosen roost** there; Charismatic must instead place **two warriors** there |

If any required action cannot be completed fully for any reason (including warrior/building supply), immediately enter **Turmoil**; do not skip that card or continue other Decree columns.

answer.ruling: No. The Decree requires two warriors for Charismatic Recruit. If only one can be placed, the required action is not fully completed and Turmoil begins immediately.

source_passages.quotation:
**Guerrilla War:** When Alliance defends, Alliance uses higher die and attacker lower; warrior caps still apply.

**Roll:** Higher die is attacker’s rolled hits, lower defender’s; equal dice give equal results. Each side’s rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle. Alliance defending reverses the dice; Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors.

answer.ruling: Alliance defending reverses dice assignment: Alliance uses higher die, attacker lower. Rolled hits remain capped by each side’s own warriors in battle; Guerrilla War does not bypass caps.

source_passages.quotation: **Supporters** are a separate face-down stack, inspectable by Alliance. They can be spent only for suit; they do not count as hand cards or toward hand limit. With no bases on map, maximum **five supporters**; incoming cards beyond capacity are discarded. With any base, unlimited supporters.

answer.ruling: Supporters separate face-down stack inspectable by Alliance; spent only for suit, not craft; not hand cards or hand limit.

source_passages.quotation: Both Revolt and Spread Sympathy take place **during Birdsong**. Complete **all Revolts before starting any Spread Sympathy**; each may be performed any number of times. Once spreading starts, you cannot return to Revolt this Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt.

answer.ruling: No. Complete all Revolts before beginning Spread; after spreading starts, cannot return to Revolt this Birdsong, so new sympathy cannot support same-Birdsong Revolt.

source_passages.quotation:
**Martial Law:** add one matching supporter if chosen clearing has at least three warriors of **one other player**.

Organize spends no supporters and has no sympathy-adjacency requirement or Martial Law cost; it still needs legal token placement.

answer.ruling: Two separate players with two warriors each do not satisfy Martial Law: target needs at least three warriors belonging to one other player. Organize has no Martial Law cost.

source_passages.quotation: Each time another player **removes sympathy** or **moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing**, that player adds one matching hand card (birds count) to Supporters. Moving a group costs one card per affected move, rather than one per warrior. Merely battling there is no trigger unless sympathy is removed; placing warriors there and moving only Vagabond pawn do not trigger it.

answer.ruling: Placing warriors there alone does not trigger Outrage; moving only Vagabond pawn does not. Moving any warriors into sympathy triggers; thus allied warriors accompanying Vagabond trigger it as a warrior move; one matching hand card per affected move.

source_passages.quotation:
**Evening:** The four military operations are **Move, Battle, Recruit and Organize**. Take **up to your number of officers** in operations, in any order and repetition. Officers stay on the board; taking an operation does not consume an officer. After operations, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard hand down to five.

| Recruit | Place one warrior at one clearing with a base |

answer.ruling: Operations are Move, Battle, Recruit, Organize; take up to officers count in any order/repetition. Officers are not consumed. Recruit puts one warrior at one base clearing. After operations, draw one plus each uncovered bonus and discard to five.

source_passages.quotation: Pawn is not a warrior, cannot rule or block rule, and cannot be removed. An enemy effect removing **all enemy pieces** from its clearing instead damages **three items**.

answer.ruling: Pawn cannot be removed. Enemy effect removing all enemy pieces from its clearing damages three Vagabond items instead.

source_passages.quotation:
**Battle:** Exhaust one sword to initiate. Maximum rolled hits, attacking or defending, equals **all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down**. As defender you are defenseless only with no undamaged swords. Take hits as item damage.

One hit damages one undamaged item of your choice; ignore excess hits when none remain.

answer.ruling: Rolled hit maximum equals all undamaged swords in Satchel whether face up or down; exhausted undamaged swords count; battle initiation still costs one ready undamaged sword. Defenseless if no undamaged swords. Hits damage one undamaged item each; ignore excess once none undamaged remain.

source_passages.quotation: Face-up tea/coins/bags in Satchel immediately move to empty matching track space if possible; each track holds at most three of its type. Exhausting an item on track sends it to Satchel. Boots/swords/crossbows/torch/hammers are gained face up in Satchel. Damaging an item sends it to Damaged box **without changing its face**. One hit damages one undamaged item of your choice; ignore excess hits when none remain. To exhaust for an action, choose a face-up **undamaged** item and flip it down. Damaged items cannot pay actions.

answer.ruling: Face-up tea/coins/bags in Satchel immediately go to empty corresponding track if possible; each track max 3. Exhausting tracked item sends it to Satchel. Damaged item goes to Damaged without changing face. Actions require face-up undamaged item; damaged cannot pay.

source_passages.quotation: 4. **Capacity, the last step of Evening after drawing and discarding:** Satchel **plus Damaged box** may contain **six items plus two per face-up bag on its track**. Track items do not count toward load. Permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within limit. Do not check capacity immediately upon acquiring an item.

answer.ruling: Satchel plus Damaged box limit = six plus two per face-up bag on bag track; track items excluded. Last Evening step after drawing/discarding, permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within capacity. No check on acquisition.

source_passages.quotation:
1. **Refresh:** First count tea **already face up on Refresh track**; flip two exhausted items face up per counted tea, then three more exhausted items. Tea refreshed during this step gives no extra refresh this step.

1. If in forest, **Rest**: return all damaged items to Satchel and flip them face up; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if able. This does not refresh undamaged exhausted items.

- **Repair:** Exhaust hammer; move one damaged item to Satchel **keeping current face**.

answer.ruling: Rest only if in forest; moves all damaged items to Satchel face up, ready tea/coins/bags to tracks. Does not flip undamaged exhausted items. Refresh flips exhausted items as specified during Birdsong; Repair costs hammer and moves one damaged item preserving face.

source_passages.quotation:
- **Aid:** Exhaust **one face-up, undamaged item of any type**, give a card matching your clearing to player with faction pieces there, even Hostile. May then take one item from their Crafted Items box face up into Satchel/track; no available item is required.

To advance a non-Hostile marker one space, Aid that faction as many times **in this same turn** as printed between current and next spaces. One Aid counts toward only one improvement. Advance and score VP printed in new space. At final space become **Allied**; each subsequent Aid to that faction scores **two VP**.

answer.ruling: Exhaust any face-up undamaged item, give a card matching clearing to faction with pieces there (even Hostile). Then may take item from its Crafted Items box, but not required. Repeated Aid in same turn counts toward relationship spaces; one Aid counts only one improvement; final Allied follow-up Aid scores 2 VP.

source_passages.quotation:
**Allied benefits:** Aid gains two VP, warriors may accompany movement, and participating warriors increase the attacking rolled-hit limit as follows:

- **Move:** May force warriors of **one** Allied faction to accompany the pawn to its destination clearing. They follow their own movement restrictions, including rule and Eyrie tie advantage. They cannot accompany a move specified to be alone. Moving them into sympathy triggers Outrage.
- **Attack with an increased hit limit:** At the start of battle **as attacker**, you may treat warriors of **one** Allied faction in the battle clearing as your own. **Add those warriors to all your undamaged swords to determine your maximum rolled hits**. They can join against a different enemy; you cannot use an ally’s warriors to attack that ally itself.

answer.ruling: Each subsequent Aid to Allied faction scores 2 VP. May force its warriors to accompany movement, following their restrictions and not on move specified alone. At battle start as attacker may use one Allied faction’s warriors to add to all undamaged swords for hit limit; may attack another enemy, cannot attack that ally.

source_passages.quotation: **Taking hits with an ally:** In a battle using Allied warriors as your own, you may absorb hits by removing those warriors or damaging your items. If you remove **more allied warriors than items you damage in that battle**, the ally becomes Hostile **at battle end**. This overrides ordinary hostility timing for those friendly warriors taken as hits against the other enemy. Equal numbers do not trigger the rule.

answer.ruling: If using allied warriors as own in battle and remove more allied warriors than Vagabond items damaged in that battle, ally becomes Hostile at battle end. Equal numbers do not.

source_passages.quotation: - **Craft:** Exhaust one hammer per crafting icon; pawn acts as crafting piece matching current clearing, and may activate repeatedly despite normal once-per-turn crafting limit. Clearing must match **all icons**; cannot craft mixed fox/rabbit/mouse requirements from one clearing. When you craft an item, you may immediately take that item face up into Satchel/track and **use it for another Daylight action immediately**, if its cost and other requirements are met. Need supply item as usual.

answer.ruling: Cannot craft fox+rabbit from one clearing because pawn must match every icon; one clearing cannot pay mixed suits. Pawn can activate repeatedly, but pay hammer per icon. If craft an item, may take face-up and immediately use for another Daylight action if cost/requirements met.

source_passages.quotation:
| Base character | Starting items | Special action |
|---|---|---|
| Thief | boot, torch, tea, sword | **Steal:** exhaust torch to take random hand card from player with faction pieces in your clearing |
| Tinker | boot, torch, bag, hammer | **Day Labor:** exhaust torch to take discard-pile card matching clearing; bird always qualifies |
| Ranger | boot, torch, crossbow, sword | **Hideout:** exhaust torch to repair three items, keeping their faces; immediately end Daylight and begin Evening |

answer.ruling: Thief starts boot/torch/tea/sword; Steal costs torch, random hand card from player with faction pieces in clearing. Tinker boot/torch/bag/hammer; Day Labor costs torch, takes discard card matching clearing (bird qualifies). Ranger boot/torch/crossbow/sword; Hideout exhaust torch, repairs three items preserving faces, ends Daylight immediately and starts Evening.

source_passages.quotation:
Ruins block their slots and can be removed only when explicitly allowed.

**Explore:** Exhaust torch in ruin’s clearing. Take one hidden item face up into Satchel or track; score one VP if an item taken. Remove ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the building slot.

answer.ruling: When last hidden item taken, remove ruin and free building slot. Ruins can only be removed when explicitly allowed; ordinary building placement cannot remove one.

source_passages.quotation: If partner wins, you also win, including if partner wins through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.

answer.ruling: Coalition partners are not enemies, so cannot be chosen as battle enemy. Coalition does not confer Allied relationship powers.

source_passages.quotation:
| Removed enemy piece | Ordinary removal VP |
|---|---|
| Warrior | **0 VP** |
| Building | **1 VP** |

**Infamy:** During battle on your own turn, score **one extra VP per hostile piece removed**, except warrior that first made faction Hostile. **Each hostile building/token removed in battle on your turn normally scores two VP: one removal VP plus one Infamy. A hostile warrior scores one Infamy, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status.**

answer.ruling: First removed non-Hostile warrior makes faction Hostile and yields zero ordinary removal VP and no Infamy for that warrior. Second warrior is Hostile and gives one Infamy VP, no ordinary warrior VP. Building yields 1 ordinary removal VP +1 Infamy =2. Total 3 VP.

source_passages.quotation:
- **Move:** Exhaust one boot, plus **one extra boot** if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction (also for forced moves).
Hostile status requires extra boot for moves into hostile warriors, not merely buildings/tokens.

answer.ruling: Hostile buildings alone add no boot: cost one boot. If destination has hostile warriors, pay one extra boot regardless of how many hostile factions/warriors; total two boots.

source_passages.quotation: During own Daylight, spend matching card to take available dominance into hand. Available **bird dominance remains bird**, so payment must be bird; a bird hand card can pay for non-bird dominance. Activation and taking are separate, neither requires a faction action allowance.

answer.ruling: Taking dominance to hand does not activate it; taking and activation are separate and neither requires faction action allowance.

source_passages.quotation: **Faction-piece ownership cannot change**: each player owns the faction chosen in setup and its listed faction pieces, except items; possessing an item does not make it faction-owned. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces.

answer.ruling: Faction-piece ownership cannot change; each player owns chosen faction and its listed faction pieces except items. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces; possessing item does not make it faction-owned.

source_passages.quotation:
- Immediate effect (paper box): resolve, then discard the **crafting card**. An item card requires the corresponding **item token** in the map supply, or it cannot be crafted. Take the item token into Crafted Items and score the VP printed on the card, subject to Eyrie exception. The item token stays; the crafting card is discarded.
- Persistent effect (stone box): keep card in your play area and gain its text, subject to personal duplicate check. Its card is outside your hand and cannot be spent/discarded/used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.

answer.ruling: Immediate-effect card resolves then is discarded; item token stays in Crafted Items. Persistent card stays in play area with effect and is outside hand, cannot be spent/discarded/used otherwise unless instructed.

source_passages.quotation: - **Ambush cards cannot be crafted:** the defender may play one for two immediate hits, or the attacker may play one to foil a defending ambush, matching the clearing. **Dominance cards cannot be crafted:** activate one to change victory condition, or spend it for suit.

answer.ruling: Neither can be crafted. Defender ambush gives two immediate hits; attacker ambush foils defending ambush, matching clearing. Dominance activates to change victory condition or is spent for suit.

source_passages.quotation:
1. Choose factions; determine starting player and seating randomly. Take faction boards and their listed pieces.
2. Put score markers at 0.
6. Distribute overview cards as desired; put battle dice nearby.
7. Set up factions in their letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. Setup order is distinct from turn order.

answer.ruling: Randomly determine starting player and seating; put score markers at zero; dice nearby. Faction setup order is Marquise/Eyrie/Alliance/Vagabond and distinct from turn order.

source_passages.quotation: **30 VP:** First to 30 wins immediately, on any player’s turn.

answer.ruling: First to 30 wins immediately on any player’s turn; no need to finish action/phase/turn.

source_passages.quotation: **Battle (4.3):** Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. **Battle does not require you to rule the clearing.**

answer.ruling: Choose a clearing where you have warriors or Vagabond pawn and an enemy to be defender. Need not rule it.

source_passages.quotation:
**Before-roll effects:** Resolve applicable effects; attacker chooses order if both have them.
**After-roll effects:** Resolve effects affecting battle that do not say “before rolling”; attacker chooses order if both have them.
The side taking hits chooses its own removal order, and chooses order of effects triggered by its pieces’ removal.

answer.ruling: Attacker chooses order for both sides’ applicable before-roll and after-roll effects when both have effects at that timing. Side taking hits chooses order of effects triggered by its own pieces’ removal.

source_passages.quotation: **Count hits:** Add extra hits (uncapped by warriors), subtract ignored hits.

answer.ruling: In Count Hits, add extra hits then subtract ignored hits.

source_passages.quotation: An item card requires the corresponding **item token** in the map supply, or it cannot be crafted. Take the item token into Crafted Items and score the VP printed on the card, subject to Eyrie exception. The item token stays; the crafting card is discarded. Ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items as Vagabond does.

answer.ruling: Non-Vagabond crafting faction takes corresponding token from map supply into its Crafted Items box, scores printed VP subject to Eyrie exception; ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items.

source_passages.quotation:
**Every crafting piece gets its suit from the clearing containing it.** The card’s **bottom-left crafting icons** require pieces of those clearing suits; the card’s own suit does not define the cost.
For **each icon**, activate **one workshop, roost or sympathy in a clearing matching that icon’s suit**, respectively. Combine eligible pieces as needed, but **each piece may activate only once per turn**.
A **three-color question-mark icon** accepts any suit.

answer.ruling: Eyrie activates roosts; Alliance sympathy. Crafting-piece suit comes from its clearing, not card suit. Three-color question mark accepts any suit. Each piece at most once per turn.

source_passages.quotation:
**Daylight:** Any order and number:
- **Craft** from hand with sympathy.
- **Mobilize:** Add one hand card to Supporters. With no base on map, keep at most five supporters and discard incoming overflow; with any base, the stack has no cap.
- **Train during Daylight:** Spend a **hand card** matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers box. Supporters cannot pay Train.

answer.ruling: Mobilize adds one hand card to Supporters; without base keep max five and discard incoming overflow; any base means no cap. Daylight Craft/Mobilize/Train in any order and number.

source_passages.quotation: **Evening, even after turmoil:** Score the VP on rightmost empty roost-track space. Draw one plus uncovered draw bonuses; discard down to five.

answer.ruling: Score VP shown on rightmost empty roost-track space, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, discard to five. This normal Evening happens after Turmoil too.

source_passages.quotation:
**Battle:** Exhaust one sword to initiate. Maximum rolled hits, attacking or defending, equals **all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down**.
To exhaust for an action, choose a face-up **undamaged** item and flip it down. Damaged items cannot pay actions.

answer.ruling: Initiating Daylight Battle exhausts one face-up undamaged sword. Exhausted undamaged sword counts toward hit maximum but cannot pay action cost because payment requires face-up undamaged.

source_passages.quotation: Take turns clockwise: **Birdsong → Daylight → Evening**.

answer.ruling: Birdsong then Daylight then Evening; turns clockwise, so next player clockwise starts after Evening.

source_passages.quotation: Damaging an item sends it to Damaged box **without changing its face**. One hit damages one undamaged item of your choice; ignore excess hits when none remain.

answer.ruling: Each hit damages one undamaged item of Vagabond’s choice; it goes to Damaged box without changing face. Already-damaged items cannot take another hit; excess hits ignored when no undamaged items remain.

source_passages.quotation:
**Evening:** The four military operations are **Move, Battle, Recruit and Organize**. Take **up to your number of officers** in operations, in any order and repetition. Officers stay on the board; taking an operation does not consume an officer.
| Recruit | Place one warrior at one clearing with a base |

answer.ruling: Up to number of officers in operations, any order/repetition; officers not consumed. One Recruit operation places one warrior at one clearing with a base.

source_passages.quotation: **Daylight:** Any order/number, as ready undamaged items permit:

answer.ruling: Vagabond Daylight allows any order and number of actions as ready undamaged items permit; no fixed action-type order, and action types may be repeated.

source_passages.quotation: - **Strike:** Exhaust crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in clearing. Only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another of its faction pieces instead.

answer.ruling: Strike exhausts one crossbow, face-up and undamaged; exhausted or damaged crossbow cannot pay.
